brief: Goldman Sachs's buyback desk recaps execution for the week ending 04-Sep-2026. Desk volumes held steady into the Labor Day weekend, tracking 1.4x the 2025 year-to-date average daily volume and 1.2x the 2024 figure, with flows concentrated in Tech, Financials and Health Care. The desk runs that volume through to a market effect: the steady corporate bid provided a supportive cushion for equities and helped absorb volatility after Friday's stronger-than-expected August jobs report triggered an S&P 500 pullback. Forward, the desk expects post-holiday volumes to hold near current levels as the corporate calendar shifts, and projects the Q3 blackout window to open around September 15, when roughly 40% of the S&P 500 enters quiet periods. That projected blackout is the stated reason execution is pivoting toward pre-set 10b5-1 programs, now 33% open market repurchase against 67% 10b5-1, versus 37% / 63% the prior week. New authorizations were light at 5 programs for $1.4B. The note states that all references to we, us and our are the views and observations of the desk rather than firm research.
